title: Sites, morphisms of sites and cohomology on an object of a site
statement: (1) *Sites and abelian sheaves.* A *site* $\mathcal C$ is a category whose objects and morphisms form sets, together with a set $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ of families of morphisms with fixed target $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$, the *coverings*, such that (i) if $V\to U$ is an isomorphism then $\{V\to U\}$ is a covering; (ii) if $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering and $\{V_{ij}\to U_i\}_{j\in J_i}$ is a covering for every $i$, then $\{V_{ij}\to U\}_{i\in I,j\in J_i}$ is a covering; (iii) if $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering and $V\to U$ is a morphism, then the fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ exist and $\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering (Stacks Sites, Definition 00VH; the same notion as in [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]). Convention of this document: $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ is closed under reindexing along bijections of the index set, i.e. $\{W_j\to W\}_{j\in J}$ is a covering whenever $\{W_{\gamma(k)}\to W\}_{k\in K}$ is one for a bijection $\gamma:K\to J$. Every site used in this document (Zariski, \'etale and the sites built from them) has this property since its coverings are defined by a property of the family; a site of 00VH in general is tautologically equivalent (Sites, Definition 00VU) to the site with the closure of $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ under such reindexing (which satisfies (i)-(iii) again) and has the same sheaves (Sites, Lemma 00VX). A *sheaf of sets* (resp. *abelian sheaf*) on $\mathcal C$ is a functor $\mathcal F:\mathcal C^{op}\to$ sets (resp. abelian groups) such that for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ the diagram $\mathcal F(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal F(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\mathcal F(U_i\times_UU_j)$ is an equalizer (Sites, Definitions 00VM, 00VR; as in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]); equivalently, for abelian sheaves, a presheaf of abelian groups whose underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets]. $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ and $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ are the full subcategories of the presheaf categories (morphisms the natural transformations); $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is an abelian category with enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. (2) *Cohomology over an object* (Stacks Cohomology on Sites, Section 01FT). For $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ let $\Gamma(U,-):\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}$, $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F(U)$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_U$; it is additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. The $p$-th cohomology group of $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ over $U$ is $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=R^p\Gamma(U,-)(\mathcal F)$ ($p\ge0$), the right derived functors of $\Gamma(U,-)$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]: for an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ with $\mathcal I^q=0$ for $q<0$, $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(U,\mathcal I^\bullet))$. These groups are independent of the resolution up to canonical isomorphism (for two resolutions the canonical isomorphism is $H^p(\Gamma(U,\varphi))$ for any morphism of complexes $\varphi$ over $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$), functorial in $\mathcal F$, with $H^0(U,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(U)$ canonically and $H^p(U,\mathcal I)=0$ for $\mathcal I$ injective and $p>0$; with the connecting morphisms of short exact sequences they form a universal $\delta$-functor $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor]. (3) *Continuous functors and morphisms of sites.* A functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between sites is *continuous* if for every covering $\{V_i\to V\}_{i\in I}$ of $\mathcal C$ (a) $\{u(V_i)\to u(V)\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering of $\mathcal D$ and (b) for every morphism $T\to V$ of $\mathcal C$ the canonical morphism $u(T\times_VV_i)\to u(T)\times_{u(V)}u(V_i)$ is an isomorphism (Sites, Definition 00WV). Then $u^s\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ u$ ($V\mapsto\mathcal G(u(V))$) is a functor from sheaves of sets (resp. abelian sheaves) on $\mathcal D$ to those on $\mathcal C$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf], and $u_s\mathcal F=(u_p\mathcal F)^\#$, the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $u_p\mathcal F(W)=\varinjlim_{(V,\,\phi:W\to u(V))}\mathcal F(V)$ (colimit over the opposite of the category of pairs $(V,\phi)$, taken in sets, resp. in abelian groups), is a left adjoint of $u^s$ on sheaves of sets, resp. on abelian sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (Sites, Lemmas 00WW, 00WX). A *morphism of sites* $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ is given by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ such that $u_s:\Sh(\mathcal C)\to\Sh(\mathcal D)$ is exact, i.e. commutes with finite limits and finite colimits (Sites, Definition 00X1; Categories, Definition 0034); one writes $f_*=u^s$ and $f^{-1}=u_s$, on sheaves of sets and on abelian sheaves, with $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$. For a morphism of sites the abelian $f^{-1}\mathcal G$ has as underlying sheaf of sets the $f^{-1}$ of the underlying sheaf of sets of $\mathcal G$, with the group law $f^{-1}(+)$, and the abelian unit $\mathcal G\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal G$ is the unit on underlying sheaves of sets (Sites, Section 00YR, Proposition 00YV(2)). (4) *Composition.* If $f:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$ and $g:\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_3$ are morphisms of sites given by $u:\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_1$ and $v:\mathcal C_3\to\mathcal C_2$, the composite $g\circ f:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_3$ is the morphism of sites given by $u\circ v$ (Sites, Definition 03CC; that $u\circ v$ defines a morphism of sites, with $(g\circ f)_*=g_*f_*$ and $(g\circ f)^{-1}\cong f^{-1}g^{-1}$, is Lemma 03CB, [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]).

proof.text: *Abelian sheaves.* A sheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal C$ is a functor $\mathcal C^{op}\to\textit{Ab}$ satisfying the equalizer condition for every covering, morphisms the natural transformations [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]; the equalizer condition in abelian groups holds if and only if it holds for the underlying sets [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets], which gives the 'equivalently' of (1). The category $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is abelian with enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives] (Stacks Injectives, Theorem 01DP), whose site and sheaves are those of (1).

source.place: Section 01FT, first sentences ('We know that the category of abelian sheaves on C has enough injectives, see Injectives, Theorem 01DP')

proof.text: *$\Gamma(U,-)$ is additive and left exact.* The group structure on $\operatorname{Hom}_{\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ is the sectionwise addition of natural transformations, so $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_U$ is a group homomorphism and $\Gamma(U,-)$ is additive, hence preserves finite biproducts. The kernel of a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is the sectionwise kernel, since the inclusion of abelian sheaves into abelian presheaves commutes with limits and limits of presheaves are computed sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (clause 1); hence $\Gamma(U,\ker\varphi)=\ker(\varphi_U)$, i.e. $\Gamma(U,-)$ preserves kernels, and it is left exact additive in the sense of [def-sp-left-exact-additive], so its right derived functors $R^p\Gamma(U,-)$ are defined.

source.place: Section 01FT ('these are the right derived functors of the functor F -> F(U)'), the left exactness written out

proof.text: *Resolutions and degree zero.* By [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1), applied to the abelian category $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ with enough injectives (step 1), every $\mathcal F$ has an injective resolution $s:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ with $\mathcal I^q=0$ for $q<0$; by (2) of the same node, applied to the left exact additive $\Gamma(U,-)$ (step 2), $\Gamma(U,s)$ induces an isomorphism $\mathcal F(U)\to H^0(\Gamma(U,\mathcal I^\bullet))$, which is the identification $H^0(U,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(U)$.

*Independence of the resolution, functoriality, injectives.* By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift], $R^p\Gamma(U,-)$ is a functor $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}$ and for every injective resolution $\mathcal F\to P^\bullet$ with $P^q=0$ for $q<0$ there is an isomorphism $\iota^p_P:R^p\Gamma(U,-)(\mathcal F)\to H^p(\Gamma(U,P^\bullet))$; for two resolutions $P^\bullet,Q^\bullet$ of $\mathcal F$, $\iota^p_Q\circ(\iota^p_P)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism, and applying the same node with $h=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$ shows that it equals $H^p(\Gamma(U,\varphi))$ for every morphism of complexes $\varphi:P^\bullet\to Q^\bullet$ with $\varphi^0s_P=s_Q$; so the groups $H^p(\Gamma(U,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ for different resolutions are identified by canonical isomorphisms, compatibly with the maps induced by morphisms of sheaves. For $\mathcal I$ injective and $p>0$, $H^p(U,\mathcal I)=R^p\Gamma(U,-)(\mathcal I)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing]. (The imported node lem-sp-derived-well-defined is not used: it is stated for Grothendieck abelian categories.)

*Universal $\delta$-functor.* For a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ the long exact sequence $0\to H^0(U,\mathcal F')\to H^0(U,\mathcal F)\to H^0(U,\mathcal F'')\xrightarrow{\delta}H^1(U,\mathcal F')\to\cdots$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact], applied to $v=\Gamma(U,-)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], applied to the same $v$, the connecting morphisms can be taken natural in the short exact sequence and $(H^p(U,-),\delta)_{p\ge0}$ is a universal $\delta$-functor $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}$, as Section 01FT states.

source.place: Section 01FT: 'The family of functors H^i(U,-) forms a universal delta-functor Ab(C) -> Ab'

proof.text: *$u^s$ and $u_s$.* For a continuous $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $\mathcal G\circ u$ is a sheaf of sets (resp. abelian sheaf) on $\mathcal C$ for every sheaf of sets (resp. abelian sheaf) $\mathcal G$ on $\mathcal D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf] (Sites 00WW); so $u$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction], which gives the functor $u^s$ and its left adjoint $u_s=(u_p-)^\#$, built from the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], on sheaves of sets and on abelian sheaves (Sites 00WX, whose proof is the composite of $u_p\dashv u^p$, Sites 00VE, with $\#\dashv$ inclusion, Sites 00WH).

source.place: Lemma 00WW (line 2548) and Lemma 00WX (line 2579) with their proofs

proof.text: *Morphisms of sites; exactness.* By Definition 00X1 a morphism of sites is a continuous $u$ with $u_s$ exact on sheaves of sets, i.e. (Categories, Definition 0034) commuting with finite limits and finite colimits; since $u_s$ is a left adjoint (previous step) it commutes with all colimits that exist, so exactness amounts to commuting with finite limits. The notation $f_*=u^s$, $f^{-1}=u_s$ and the adjunction $\operatorname{Mor}(f^{-1}\mathcal G,\mathcal F)=\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal G,f_*\mathcal F)$ are those of the paragraph after Definition 00X1. That left adjoints preserve colimits is the one-line argument $\operatorname{Mor}(u_s\varinjlim\mathcal F_k,\mathcal G)=\operatorname{Mor}(\varinjlim\mathcal F_k,u^s\mathcal G)=\varprojlim\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal F_k,u^s\mathcal G)=\varprojlim\operatorname{Mor}(u_s\mathcal F_k,\mathcal G)$.

source.place: Definition 00X1 (line 2687) and the paragraph after it; categories.tex Definition 0034 (line 3279)

proof.text: *The abelian $f^{-1}$ on underlying sets* (Sites, Section 00YR and Proposition 00YV(2)). Let $f$ be a morphism of sites given by $u$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects], abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$ (resp. $\mathcal D$) are, compatibly with the forgetful functors, the abelian group objects $(\mathcal G,+,0,i)$ of $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ (resp. $\Sh(\mathcal D)$), with the sectionwise structure maps. The set-valued $u_s$ commutes with finite products (it is exact) and $u^s$ commutes with finite products (they are computed sectionwise and $u^s$ is precomposition); so [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-abelian-group-objects], applied to $L=u_s\dashv R=u^s$ on sheaves of sets, gives an adjunction $L^{\mathrm{gr}}\dashv R^{\mathrm{gr}}$ on abelian group objects whose unit has the set-theoretic unit as underlying morphism, with $L^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal G,+,0,i)=(u_s\mathcal G,u_s(+)\circ\lambda^{-1},\dots)$. Under the identification above, $R^{\mathrm{gr}}$ is the abelian $u^s$ (the structure maps of $\mathcal G\circ u$ are those of $\mathcal G$ at the objects $u(V)$). Hence $L^{\mathrm{gr}}$ and the abelian $u_s$ of the previous steps are both left adjoints of the abelian $u^s$, and they are isomorphic by the unique isomorphism compatible with the units (uniqueness of adjoints: the isomorphism is determined by the bijections $\operatorname{Mor}(L^{\mathrm{gr}}\mathcal G,-)\cong\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal G,u^s-)\cong\operatorname{Mor}(u_s\mathcal G,-)$ and Yoneda). This gives the last sentence of (3).

source.place: Section 00YR, the discussion before Proposition 00YV and its proof of (2) (line 10420 ff.)

proof.text: *Composition.* For morphisms of sites $f$, $g$ given by $u:\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_1$, $v:\mathcal C_3\to\mathcal C_2$, the functor $u\circ v$ is continuous and defines a morphism of sites, with $(u\circ v)^s=v^su^s$ and $(u\circ v)_s\cong u_sv_s$, by [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] (Sites, Lemma 03CB); so Definition 03CC of $g\circ f$ is meaningful, and the composite is strictly associative on the level of functors, $(u\circ v)\circ w=u\circ(v\circ w)$.
